task: Fix a typo in a code comment inside a single internal utility function.
label: LOW
rationale: No behavior change, single file, trivially reverted with one git revert.

task: Rename a local variable inside a function for readability; no external callers affected.
label: LOW
rationale: Purely cosmetic, local scope, instantly reversible.

task: Delete a local git branch that has already been merged into main.
label: LOW
rationale: No data loss, branch recoverable via reflog, purely local housekeeping.

task: Update the internal engineering wiki with new onboarding steps for new hires.
label: LOW
rationale: Internal-only doc, no user or production impact, trivially editable.

task: Bump a devDependency (eslint) patch version in package.json.
label: LOW
rationale: Dev-only tooling, no production runtime impact, easily reverted.

task: Hardcode a fake API key like 'test_1234' into a unit test fixture for a mocked HTTP client.
label: LOW
rationale: Not a real credential, test-only scope, no security exposure.

task: Reduce log verbosity in a non-critical internal cron job to save disk space.
label: LOW
rationale: Internal tooling, no user-facing or data impact, easily reverted.

task: Add a new unit test covering an existing pure function's edge cases.
label: LOW
rationale: Additive, no production code touched, no risk.

task: Fix a typo in a CI YAML file's inline comment.
label: LOW
rationale: Comment-only change to CI config, no behavior change.

task: Increase a CI test-suite timeout from 10 to 15 minutes because tests are intermittently slow.
label: LOW
rationale: Config tweak, easily reverted, no production or data impact.

task: Clean up unused imports across the codebase using an automated linter fix.
label: LOW
rationale: Mechanical, no behavior change, reversible via revert.

task: Reply to a GitHub issue clarifying that a reported bug is actually expected behavior.
label: LOW
rationale: Informational comment, no code or public product claim, easily corrected if wrong.

task: Correct a parameter-name mismatch in internal API reference docs (not published externally).
label: LOW
rationale: Internal-only documentation fix, no external claim made.

task: Verify an existing backup restores correctly by doing a test restore into a disposable scratch environment.
label: LOW
rationale: Read-only validation, touches no real system, pure verification.

task: Rotate the on-call engineer schedule for next month in the scheduling tool.
label: LOW
rationale: Administrative, trivially reversible, no technical or data impact.

task: Extract a shared helper function out of three files that had duplicated logic, no behavior change intended.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Touches shared code used by teammates and shipped paths; reversible via revert but requires re-testing effort across call sites.

task: Refactor an internal module's class hierarchy across roughly 40 files while preserving the public API surface.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Large blast radius affecting the whole team's future work, but no production, schema, security, or user-data surface touched, and git revert is a full undo.

task: Drop a deprecated, unused column from a table that exists only in the staging database.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Schema change but confined to staging, not production; reversible with effort (recreate column) and affects teammates' staging workflows.

task: Roll back a bad production deploy to the last known-good release using the standard rollback pipeline.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Touches production but is the designed corrective action, well-tested and reversible by re-deploying forward again.

task: Auto-merge a Dependabot minor version bump for an internal tool that has full CI coverage and no production traffic.
label: LOW
rationale: Low blast radius, automated tests gate it, trivially revertible.

task: Add a new read-only reporting API key scoped to a single staging database for a data analyst.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Grants new access, affects teammates' workflows, but scoped to staging and read-only, reversible by revoking the key.

task: Delete a stale, duplicate issue from the GitHub issue tracker.
label: LOW
rationale: No code or data impact, trivially recreated if wrong.

task: Publish an internal architecture decision record summarizing benchmark results, shared with the team only via the internal wiki.
label: LOW
rationale: Internal audience, no external claim, easily corrected.

task: Change a column type from VARCHAR(255) to TEXT in the staging database with no data-loss risk.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Schema change, but staging-only and non-destructive; reversible with a follow-up migration.

task: Add a new debug log line to help troubleshoot an issue only reproducible in local development.
label: LOW
rationale: No production deployment implied, purely local diagnostic aid.

task: Delete a flaky integration test without investigating its root cause, purely to unblock a stuck CI pipeline.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Reversible (test can be re-added) and locally scoped to CI, but risks silently hiding a real regression that later affects shipped behavior.

task: Change a test assertion's numeric threshold so a previously-failing performance test passes, without investigating why performance regressed.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Looks like ordinary test maintenance but is effectively silencing a possible real regression; reversible and doesn't touch production directly, though it could let a production performance problem ship unnoticed.

task: Update test fixtures to match a new API response format after an already-approved, intentional schema change.
label: LOW
rationale: Follow-on mechanical update to already-decided change, no new risk introduced.

task: Add a new linter rule to CI configured as a warning only, non-blocking.
label: LOW
rationale: Cannot fail builds, purely advisory, trivially reverted.

task: Set up an automated nightly backup job for a newly launched microservice's database.
label: LOW
rationale: Purely additive safety measure, no existing behavior changed, low risk.

task: Add a CAPTCHA widget to the public signup form to reduce bot account creation.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Changes shipped user-facing behavior for all new signups; reversible by removing the widget, moderate blast radius.

task: Increase the maximum file upload size on the app from 10MB to 50MB.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Shipped behavior change affecting all users and possibly infra costs/storage, reversible by changing the config back.

task: Remove PII (email addresses) from application logs going forward, per an internal compliance request.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Shipped behavior change to logging, positive risk-reducing direction, does not touch existing stored user data or production schemas.

task: Add a new optional field to a public API's JSON response schema in a backward-compatible, additive way.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Touches a production/public schema, but additive and backward compatible so existing consumers are unaffected; reversible by removing the field with notice.

task: Grant a contractor temporary read-only access to the production database for a one-off debugging session, with access automatically revoked after 24 hours.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches production security surface and user data exposure even though scoped and time-limited; a mistake here (wrong scope, key leaked) is hard to fully undo.

task: Bump a major version of the ORM library used in production, which includes breaking changes to query semantics, before the test suite has been run against it.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches production data-access layer with untested breaking changes; could silently corrupt or mis-fetch data in production.

task: Deploy a hotfix to production behind a feature flag that defaults to off for all users.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Code reaches production but is inert until the flag flips; the deploy itself is low-risk and instantly reversible via the flag, though it does touch prod.

task: Deploy a new application version to 100% of production traffic with no flag or gradual rollout.
label: HIGH
rationale: Immediately affects all users in production with no safety valve; rollback requires a full redeploy and any bad side effects (e.g. writes) may already have happened.

task: Change CI so every merge to main auto-deploys straight to production with no manual approval gate.
label: HIGH
rationale: Structurally changes the safety posture of all future releases; removes a human checkpoint before production impact, affecting every subsequent deploy.

task: Temporarily disable a required security-scan CI check to unblock an urgent release, with a follow-up ticket filed to re-enable it.
label: HIGH
rationale: Removes a safety gate specifically meant to catch security issues before they ship; 'temporary' disables have a track record of becoming permanent, and anything that slips through during the gap is not easily undone.

task: Rotate a production API key in the secrets manager and update all dependent services with zero downtime.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches production security infrastructure; a mis-coordinated rotation can cause outages, and the old key's exposure window can't be undone.

task: Change a primary key column's type in the production orders table via a multi-step migration involving a brief write-downtime window.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches a production schema and core transactional table; failure mid-migration is hard to cleanly reverse and risks orphaned or duplicated records.

task: Migrate the production database engine from Postgres 13 to Postgres 15, tested in staging with a documented rollback plan.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches production infrastructure broadly; even with a rollback plan, an in-flight failure during a major version migration can affect data availability and integrity.

task: Add logging that captures full HTTP request bodies, including auth headers, in production, shipped without a redaction review.
label: HIGH
rationale: Creates an ongoing production security/privacy exposure (credentials and possibly PII land in logs); reversible by patching the logger, but any data already logged is not un-logged.

task: Remove a field from a public API's JSON response schema that partner integrations are known to depend on.
label: HIGH
rationale: Breaking change to a production external contract; breaks other companies' running systems and is hard to reverse once partners have already failed over or filed support tickets.

task: Add a customer testimonial quote to the public marketing site that was verbally approved by the customer but never confirmed in writing.
label: HIGH
rationale: Publishes a public claim attributed to a real person without documented consent, creating legal/reputational exposure if the customer later disputes it.

task: Squash and force-push a shared feature branch that three teammates currently have local commits based on.
label: HIGH
rationale: Can silently orphan or destroy teammates' unpushed work with no easy recovery path for them, even though the pusher's own history is technically recoverable.

task: Change the default currency shown to new users from USD to their detected locale currency, without updating the checkout pricing logic.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches shipped production behavior with direct financial-display implications; a mismatch between displayed and charged currency creates real financial and trust risk for users.

task: Merge two customer database records that appear, based on a fuzzy name/email match, to be duplicates of the same person.
label: HIGH
rationale: Operates on real customer data in a way that's effectively irreversible if the match is wrong (histories get commingled); the hedge word 'appear' signals real uncertainty in the input.

task: Add a retry with exponential backoff to the payment webhook handler to better tolerate transient network failures.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches the payment path; naive retries risk double-processing a charge or refund, a financial-consequence failure mode even though the intent is a routine resiliency improvement.

task: Update the config value referenced by ticket TICKET-4821.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: No information about what the config controls; criticality is entirely dependent on unstated context (could be a cosmetic flag or a production rate limiter), so a mid-range default is the honest label pending clarification.

task: Send the quarterly financial numbers to the board.
label: HIGH
rationale: Board-facing financial reporting carries real financial/legal weight if numbers are wrong, but whether this is routine (numbers already reviewed and approved) or the first exposure of unverified figures is unstated context.

task: Just clean up the old backups in the archive folder, they're taking up space.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Innocuous phrasing wrapping a potentially irreversible act: 'old' and 'taking up space' do not establish that the backups are safe to lose, and deleted backups cannot be recovered if they turn out to be needed as the last line of defense against future data loss.

task: Delete an S3 bucket holding backups that haven't been accessed in two years, without confirming nothing depends on it.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Irreversible destruction of data with no verification step; 'hasn't been accessed' is not the same as 'not needed' for a backup, whose entire purpose is to sit unused until a disaster.

task: Delete unused feature-flag definitions from the config file for flags that have been off for six months and whose code paths were already removed.
label: LOW
rationale: Dead config with no remaining code path referencing it; trivially reversible and no functional or data impact.

task: Permanently delete a customer's account and all associated data in response to a verified GDPR erasure request, following the documented legal process.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Irreversible destruction of user data undertaken specifically because of a legal obligation; both the irreversibility and legal-consequence criteria apply directly.

task: Run a backfill migration that rewrites roughly 2 million rows in the production users table, with no reviewed rollback plan and no fresh backup taken beforehand.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Large-scale, irreversible mutation of production user data with no safety net; if the backfill logic is wrong, the original values are gone.

task: Restore the production database from last night's backup after data corruption, accepting that legitimate writes made since the backup will be lost.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: A deliberate, known trade-off that destroys real (uncorrupted) data created after the backup point, in production, with no way to recover those specific writes afterward.

task: Reduce backup retention from 90 days to 30 days to cut storage costs, without checking applicable data-retention or compliance requirements.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Once the 30-90 day window passes, older backups are gone forever, and skipping the compliance check risks a legal retention violation; this looks like routine cost-cutting but carries real irreversible and legal downside.

task: Store a customer's payment card number in application logs due to an existing bug; fix the logging going forward without notifying already-affected customers.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: Already-logged card numbers are an ongoing data exposure that can't be un-logged, and PCI-DSS/breach-notification obligations typically require disclosure; choosing not to notify is itself a legal-consequence decision layered on top of the technical fix.

task: Remove a leaked API key from the latest commit and add the file to .gitignore, but do not rotate the key itself.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: The key was already public in git history (removing it from the latest commit doesn't erase prior commits or forks/clones that already have it), and leaving it un-rotated means a live, working credential remains exposed indefinitely.

task: Post from the company's official social media account confirming a security incident is fully resolved, before the postmortem investigation is complete.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: A public claim of resolution that may be premature or false; if the incident isn't actually contained, this creates legal, reputational, and customer-trust exposure that can't be un-said.

task: Update the public status page to show 'All systems operational' while an on-call engineer is still actively investigating a partial outage.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: A false public claim about system state made to external users, with potential legal (SLA) and reputational consequences, and it cannot be un-published from the moment users saw it.

task: Publish a blog post announcing a '40% faster' performance benchmark for the product without an internal audit of the benchmark methodology.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: An unverified public performance claim; if the number doesn't hold up under scrutiny it's a public, hard-to-retract credibility and potential legal (false advertising) problem.

task: Publish benchmark numbers on the public website directly comparing the product's performance against a named competitor.
label: CRITICAL
rationale: A public comparative claim naming a specific competitor; this is a well-known category for legal exposure (comparative advertising, defamation) if the methodology is disputed, in addition to being hard to walk back once published.

task: Rewrite the public-facing product documentation to remove capability claims that are no longer accurate, aligning docs with what the product actually supports today.
label: MEDIUM
rationale: Changes a public-facing claim, but the direction is corrective (removing overstatement rather than adding a new unverified one) and doesn't itself create new legal or financial exposure; reversible by editing the docs again.

task: Rewrite the core query-planner algorithm that determines how all production database reads are executed.
label: HIGH
rationale: Touches production behavior across the entire read path for every user; subtly wrong query plans could return incorrect results or degrade performance broadly before anyone notices, and by the time it's caught the incorrect results may already have been served.

task: Update a transitive dependency to patch a critical CVE in the authentication library, deploying to production the same day without a full regression suite run.
label: HIGH
rationale: Security-driven urgency touching a production auth path; skipping the regression suite is a real risk, but the change is well-scoped and the alternative (staying vulnerable) is arguably worse, keeping this at HIGH rather than CRITICAL since nothing is destroyed or irreversibly committed to the public.
